newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Preliminary census results show that South Africa's population is smaller, more urbanised and younger than previously thought.

- The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has given the go-ahead for a billion-dollar global satellite telephone network whose construction and launch depends heavily on a South African empowerment group contributing a pledged $350 million.
- Gross reserve figures for June came in well below expectations at 22.1 billion rand, from 21.8 billion rand in May.
- A dispute between Liberty Life and other Life Offices' Association members has been settled in a move interpreted within the industry as being a climbdown by the association.
- Northern Province Premier Ngoako Ramatlhodi has sacked half of his cabinet in a reshuffle which draws most of his significant inner-party opponents into the government.

- The introduction of a land tax, a "one-man one farm" law and bans on ownership by foreigners or foreign companies of agricultural land were among measures announced by Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe when he opened parliament on Tuesday.
- South Africans invested just 15 million rand abroad on Tuesday, after the much-talked-about relaxation of exchange controls, Reserve Bank deputy governor James Cross said.
- Three road construction projects worth more than 3.4 billion rand and capable of creating at least 100,000 jobs were announced by Transport Minister Mac Maharaj.
- Gold continued to weaken on international markets on Tuesday, hitting $333.60 an ounce.
- Construction, engineering and transport group Murray and Roberts warned shareholders that it expected to report an attributable loss of about 275 million rand for the year to June 30.
